text: The reality is that there is a very high volume of people and goods that cross our border, and so, it is not feasible for us to check or to subject each and every person, and each and every vehicle to extensive checks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: But that said, CNB works closely with the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) on joint operations and conduct intel-led checks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: CNB also shares information on latest regional drug trends and modus operandi of trafficking syndicates.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: CNB also collaborates with partners across the world, including the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department of the Royal Malaysian Police and the International Criminal Police Organization (INTERPOL) to investigate and dismantle cross-border drug trafficking syndicates.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Members have also spoken about how the Internet facilitates cross-border drug trafficking.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will continue to maintain the tough laws against trafficking across all mediums, whether the offence is facilitated via physical meetups or the Internet.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Ms Joan Pereira asked whether our intelligence teams are empowered to access encrypted messages.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: CNB uses its forensic capabilities to extract and access encrypted information in suspects' phones and computers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: On the issue of cannabis, when dealing with the international drug situation, enforcement is only part of the story.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The battle for the hearts and minds is equally tough, and thus, we have been stepping up on our Preventive Drug Education (PDE).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: As Mr Christopher de Souza and Ms Irene Quay observed, other countries have softened their approach towards cannabis.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Our children can be misled into thinking that cannabis is harmless.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We make sure we provide such timely reminders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: In December last year, I launched a storybook with an anti-drug message for lower primary school children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The books are available at public libraries and primary schools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: CNB works closely with MOE to provide PDE throughout primary, secondary and tertiary education.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: As Er Dr Lee Bee Wah observed, fundamentally, our children need perceptiveness and resilience against drug misinformation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We also know how important peer influence is, and so, CNB has set up an Anti-drug Abuse Advocacy Network comprising more than 500 youth leaders, educators, influencers and other members of the community, who use their voices to help encourage others to lead drug-free lives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: As Mr Mohamed Irshad mentioned, NS is another important touchpoint.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Besides educating servicemen in both Home Team and SAF through mandatory talks, commanders are also equipped with PDE toolkits that they can use to educate servicemen on drug abuse.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The National Council Against Drug Abuse has a DrugFreeSG Fund that organisations can tap on for funding support of anti-drug initiatives, including awareness campaigns and ad hoc activities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: By continuously engaging youths at various stages of their development, we want them to internalise the facts about the harms of drugs, so that they will be smart and resist bad influence and reject misinformation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will also continue to study others' best practices to see what we can improve, for example, the Icelandic Model, which promotes dialogue among those in research, policy and practice.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The National Committee on Prevention, Rehabilitation and Recidivism set up in April 2018 is one such avenue to bring together policymakers, practitioners and researchers to co-create solutions to prevent offending, reoffending and enhance rehabilitation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: With the inclusion of cannabis in many non-medicinal products sold overseas like cigarettes and oils, Ms Irene Quay also asked about how we can ensure the general public are well-informed of risks when they travel overseas.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: CNB issues public advisories to remind the public of these risks and not to bring in cannabis products.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will continue to do so via traditional and social media platforms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: CNB also closely monitors the importation and sale of cannabis products in Singapore and will take tough actions against those who engage in these activities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Ms Irene Quay asked how we handle travellers who are legitimately prescribed with scheduled drugs if they intend to enter Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Travellers visiting Singapore are allowed to bring in or import their prescribed medications, but depending on the specific type, an approval to import is required before the person arrives in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Detailed information and application procedures can be found on HSA's website.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: As Mr Pritam Singh has said, it is important that the general population, and even foreigners, are aware of our laws, including new ones, and we will continue to expand our outreach efforts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: On New Psychoactive Substances (NPS), this is another global challenge with the rapid emergence of NPS, and this is what Mr Christopher de Souza had spoken about.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Syndicates and rogue chemists quickly churn modified products, marketing them as a safe and legal high, profiting off others' misery.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: MHA has been proactive in listing NPS as controlled drugs under the MDA.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza and Ms Anthea Ong asked about the medical observation period of up to seven days.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Such medical observation is for the purpose of determining whether a person has consumed drugs and is meant to provide legal clarity for existing practices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This period is for doctors to observe the person, like his withdrawal symptoms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: As to how fast this appears is dependent on the type of drug and how heavily addicted the suspected abuser is, and when he last consumed the drugs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Ms Irene Quay also asked if there are plans to consider dispensing separation for controlled drugs and other drugs like hypnotics and codeine-containing preparations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: MOH currently manages the risk of errant prescription by practitioners through legislative controls, guidelines in supply, prescription and dispensing of drugs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This is coupled with random ad hoc audits of the records of the dispensing of drugs in licensed healthcare institutions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Dr Intan Mokhtar asked how the SAF deals with drug abuse.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: MINDEF and the SAF take a zero-tolerance approach towards drug abuse and work closely with CNB to deal with drug abuse in the SAF.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu asked about appeal processes for those charged with drug offences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The processes are no different from other appeal processes and an application can be filed with the Courts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: (In Malay):   This is an important amendment that will help to enhance our whole strategy in the fight against drugs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This allows them to be supervised but also gives them an opportunity to get a stable job and improve relations with their families and society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Second, we will target acts of contamination to strongly deter behaviour that can propagate drug abuse and harm others.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: For example, it is an offence to teach others how to take part in drug activities like taking drugs, making drugs and distributing drugs, with the knowledge that the person intends to carry out those activities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I agree with the suggestions from Dr Intan Mokhtar, Ms Rahayu Mahzam and Mr Faisal Manap about the dangers of drugs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Drug abuse can destroy families and have a significant impact on the children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Together with our community partners, we will work towards freeing Singapore from the drug scourge.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Everyone who spoke welcomed the Bill and it was across party lines.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I will just deal with a couple of points which are slightly more philosophical or, perhaps, a matter of principle.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: First, is Mr Pritam Singh's point going back to the speech when the LT regime was introduced in 1998.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The LT regime – LT1/LT2 – was introduced at a point when the situation was quite dire.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We had about, I think, between 7,000 and 8,000 in DRC.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Three quarters of them were hardcore opiate users.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They repeatedly went back to heroin, morphine, opium and many were using crime to feed their habit.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I can talk about a few other factors but, essentially, we were facing a very difficult situation.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And if we did not deal with it decisively, the sense was that it could have gotten much worse.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In the context of the very serious concerns that the Ministry then had, the LT regime was conceptualised.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The proposals received very strong support from Members and the larger community, and also the people who worked with the addicts.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They were very concerned because they could see that many of the addicts they were working with did not change their attitudes.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, decisive action had to be taken, it was taken, and what the LT regime did was to keep away from society many of the hardcore users who could have infected many others, who could have induced many others to come into the drug trade and drug abuse situation.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, together with strong enforcement, more preventive education, improvements in rehabilitation and the LT regime, I think we dealt effectively with the situation.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, you can say, roughly, it has fallen by half.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, we are in a much better situation, but we are in this situation because of the actions that had been taken in the past.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Mr Pritam Singh is right in asking the question.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The profile of the abusers over the 20 years has changed with the profile change of the general population as a whole, though I do not have the figures right here to give.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The other point is that the drugs of choice have changed as well, from the very hardcore heroin to more NPS and so on.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Again, a different situation, compared with what we had 20 years ago; many with higher educational qualifications, professionals, and many of them use drugs like "Ice" and NPS.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: As Mr Pritam Singh and other Members have said, it is not without risks.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: One of the risks is, of course, how people might characterise it.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But people must be slow to characterise the Singapore Government as being weak or soft on drugs.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Some people might take that view, but I think we have to do the right thing.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The knowledge and experience built up over the last 20 years enable us to take a risk-based approach which, as far as possible, take into consideration an individual's risk and protective factors, so that the intervention is most effective and appropriate.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But we will continue to take an evidence-based approach.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We will see what is it that we can improve, and we will have no hesitation in refining or even changing our policies based on evidence.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If I may deal now with the points – again, slightly more philosophical in nature – raised by Nominated Member of Parliament Ms Anthea Ong.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: She suggested that it is a habit to do with brain structure and could be beyond people's control.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I think it will be wrong of the Government to say we will not consider certain things or we will not accept certain things.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It is not a hard line which precludes consideration of evidence.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We have to, when we deal with public policy, deal with evidence and base our policies on evidence and science.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But I will caution against taking approaches which are fashionable – I am not suggesting the approaches the Member suggests are fashionable – and which have been thoroughly discredited if you have looked at the evidence from the countries which have taken that approach.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I think their experience shows these approaches to be thoroughly discredited.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We will be quite stupid if we blindly follow because the arguments are attractive but not backed by evidence.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, I think there is scope for saying that we will look at research, we will look at evidence, and we will manage our policies accordingly.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: At the same time, we also have to believe in individual responsibility until evidence shows us otherwise.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The suggestion that we have to put human beings in the centre of our policies, I do not think we can agree more.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Though, if I could decode what Ms Anthea Ong was saying, I think, in context, she was talking about the drug abuser and putting that human being at the centre of our policies, which is usually how debates in this field are often structured.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: When I say I agree completely, I would add this caveat that I will put also the victims of the drugs at the heart of our policies.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And, usually, the victims far outnumber the drug.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The drug abusers are victims, the drug traffickers, in some way, are the people who are benefiting from it.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But there are a lot of people who are innocent bystanders who suffer as a result of other people's drug habits.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: These people do not find mention in many of these debates which centre on drugs.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: A few years ago, there was a little girl – I think she must have been four or five – called Noi Noi, charming, a life full of hope and expectation.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Her adult relative, a drug abuser, killed her.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: She does not enter the statistics in the context of debates on drug abuse.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The reason why – and I have said this many times, for those of us who have children – you will let your 10-year-old child go on public transport in Singapore but you will not let that child take public transport in many other first-world cities is because we are safe, and we are safe because of our drug policies.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Let us not be seduced by the liberal arguments.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Where it makes good sense, we will take it, as Members can see from major aspects of this policy.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But where it makes sense, we must be ready to stand our ground.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, we want to achieve the core goal of reducing drug abuse in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: As Mr Desmond Choo, Mr Pritam Singh and other Members pointed out, there is a risk of these changes being characterised as we are going soft.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We will distinguish between abusers who only consume drugs from those who also face charges for other offences and we will point out that the approach we are taking is based on evidence.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It is not going hard or going soft.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There is no particular merit in being hard for the sake of being hard or soft for the sake of being soft, or attaching labels like right-wing, left-wing, liberal.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: What is relevant is the evidence, how we deal with it, what is in the interest of our society.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And we deal with it openly and debate it openly.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We set out the facts and we try and come to an agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Those who face additional charges for other offences will continue to be charged for their drug consumption offences as well as their other offences.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We will do this in a measured, targeted fashion.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We have to give the next generation the best chance of leading a drug-free life.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Together, we will continue to work towards maintaining a drug-free Singapore.
